# BucketDB

TypeScript document database (version 0.4.0-beta.0). Uses AWS S3 / Alibaba Cloud OSS / local filesystem / memory as backend. No database server, no runtime dependencies. Requires Node >= 20 or Bun.

## Key concepts

- `BucketDB` — `new BucketDB(adapter, dbPath)`; `dbPath` is a key prefix (`''` = bucket root, may contain `/`)
- `Collection<T>` — typed collection, returned by `db.collection<T>(name)` (same instance per name)
- Storage: one JSON object per document at `<dbPath>/<collection>/docs/<id>.json`. No index, no log, no query cache.
- Every document extends `Document`: `id` (UUID, taken from the object key), `_etag` (from storage, not stored in the body), `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt`
- `InsertDocument<T>` and `UpdateDocument<T>` exclude `id`, `_etag`, `_createdAt`, `_updatedAt` (UpdateDocument is also Partial); system fields passed at runtime are dropped
- Optimistic locking: `update(id, data, { etag: doc._etag })`; stale etag or lost race throws ConcurrentUpdateError (no retry). Works on Memory, S3, and FileSystem within one process. On OSS, update with etag throws UnsupportedError.
- update without etag: on Memory / FileSystem (one process) / S3, conflicting writes are retried (up to 5 retries) so concurrent partial updates all apply; on OSS last writer wins.

## Guarantees per backend

|                                      | Memory | FileSystem             | S3  | OSS                              |
|--------------------------------------|--------|------------------------|-----|----------------------------------|
| single write atomic                  | yes    | yes                    | yes | yes                              |
| create-if-absent (insert)            | yes    | yes (across processes) | yes | yes (non-versioned buckets only) |
| conditional update (etag)            | yes    | single process only    | yes | no — UnsupportedError            |
| concurrent partial updates all apply | yes    | single process         | yes | no (last writer wins)            |

Multiple writer processes are supported for insert/delete on every backend and for update on S3 (Memory/FileSystem: within one process).

## Limitations (0.4.0-beta.0)

- No transactions; each write touches one document.
- Every find lists the collection and GETs every document (16 in parallel), then filters in memory; only `{ id: '...' }` reads one document. No benchmarks yet; no capacity is claimed. Intended for small collections (thousands of documents) and a few writes per second.
- OSS: no conditional update (etag → UnsupportedError); concurrent etag-less updates are last-writer-wins.
- FileSystem: etag checks / concurrent update merging hold only within one process.
- 0.3.x and 0.4 clients must not write the same collection concurrently. 0.4 reads 0.3 data as-is; it reads nothing outside `docs/` and skips 0.3's `*.meta` files, so 0.3's index and log directories can be deleted.
- Beta: API may change before 0.4.0.

## Package: @hold-baby/bucket-db

### Exports

Classes: BucketDB, Collection, MemoryStorageAdapter, FileSystemAdapter, S3Adapter, OSSAdapter
Errors: BucketDBError, ValidationError, DocumentNotFoundError, ConcurrentUpdateError, UnsupportedError, StorageError
Types: Document, InsertDocument, UpdateDocument, QueryOperator, QueryValue, QueryFilter, QueryOptions, UpdateOptions, FileSystemAdapterConfig, S3AdapterOptions, OSSAdapterOptions, Credentials, CredentialProvider, StorageAdapter, Capabilities, Guarantee, WriteCondition, ObjectEntry, ListPage, ListOptions, StorageErrorKind, StorageErrorOptions

### Collection API

```
insert(data: InsertDocument<T>): Promise<T>                 // 1 conditional PUT, generated UUID id
findById(id: string): Promise<T | null>                     // 1 GET; null ONLY if missing, other storage errors throw
find(filter?: QueryFilter<T>, options?: QueryOptions): Promise<T[]>   // LIST + GET all; results in id (key) order
update(id: string, data: UpdateDocument<T>, options?: UpdateOptions): Promise<T>   // GET + conditional PUT
delete(id: string): Promise<void>                           // 1 DELETE; no error if missing
```

### QueryOptions / UpdateOptions

```
{ limit?: number, offset?: number }   // applied after filtering
{ etag?: string }
```

### Query operators

$eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in, $nin (fields combined with AND). Unknown operators, non-array $in/$nin, reserved field names (constructor, __proto__, …) throw ValidationError.

### Adapters

```
new MemoryStorageAdapter()
new FileSystemAdapter({ basePath })
new S3Adapter({ bucket, region?, endpoint?, credentials?, forcePathStyle?, timeoutMs? })
new OSSAdapter({ bucket, region?, endpoint?, credentials?, timeoutMs? })
credentials: { accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken?, expiresAt? } | (() => Promise<that>)   // provider re-called 5 min before expiresAt
```

S3 defaults: region AWS_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION; endpoint AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3 / AWS_ENDPOINT_URL / https://s3.<region>.amazonaws.com; credentials AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN. Any S3-compatible service via endpoint; only AWS S3 and OSS are tested.
OSS defaults: region OSS_REGION (`cn-hangzhou`; `oss-cn-hangzhou` also accepted); endpoint https://s3.oss-<region>.aliyuncs.com (S3-compatible; OSS_ENDPOINT is not read); credentials OSS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / OSS_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET / OSS_SESSION_TOKEN.
Path-style addressing is automatic for IP/localhost endpoints.
Retries (S3 and OSS): up to 3 attempts, per-attempt timeout 10 s (timeoutMs), on network errors, timeouts, 5xx, 429, SlowDown, RequestTimeout.

### Error mapping

ValidationError        — invalid collection name / document ID / dbPath segment / filter; invalid adapter options; missing credentials
DocumentNotFoundError  — update on a missing doc
ConcurrentUpdateError  — update with stale etag, lost race with etag, or etag-less update retries exhausted
UnsupportedError       — backend lacks the capability (OSS update with etag)
StorageError           — storage failure; fields kind ('not-found' | 'conflict' | 'transient' | 'permanent'), key, status. Also thrown by find for a file under docs/ that is not `<id>.json` holding a JSON object (key names the file). Hidden files (starting with `.`) are ignored.
All extend BucketDBError.

Names: collection names, document IDs and each `/`-separated dbPath segment must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]{1,255}$ and not start with `.`; otherwise ValidationError (never rewritten).
